comparison.objective: Distinct: reset loose tongue-and-groove pliers from groove 1 to groove 5 and leave them flat, versus commission and lock a robot-axis damper through repeated guarded impact cycles.
comparison.physical_skill: Pliers require opening a hinged tool past 72°, sliding its joint 24 mm, reseating the tongue, and releasing it. Candidate requires recessed hex-key engagement, setscrew loosening/retightening, counterholding, fine collar rotation, physical cycle-control actuation, and feedback-driven adjustment from dynamic impacts. Generic bimanual stabilization is the only material shared primitive.
comparison.success_condition: Pliers: groove-5 seating within 1.5 mm, withstand a 5 N lock test with under 1 mm motion, lie flat and untouched for 1 s. Candidate: two consecutive ≥0.85 J cycles within the rated velocity range, ≤12 mm piston travel, no hard-stop strike/bottoming/overload/excessive rebound, and retained collar setting after witness torque. Candidate omits numeric thresholds for excessive rebound, overload, and collar-drift tolerance, but these gaps do not plausibly make it the pliers-reset task.
comparison.reason: The tested ability changes from one-shot passive hand-tool joint reconfiguration to tool-mediated locking plus iterative dynamic-response commissioning under energy, stroke, rebound, and retention constraints. Both complete indexed spec versions were read and describe the same pliers task; geometry or industrial naming is not the basis for this distinction.
